claims.text: The nanoparticles are equiatomic Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Cu high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
The as-prepared nanoparticles form a homogeneous solid solution.
The as-prepared nanoparticles possess measurable lattice strain caused by atomic-size mismatch.
Atomic-size mismatch among Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Cu induces internal lattice strain.
Internal lattice strain increases the energy barrier for atomic diffusion.
An increased diffusion barrier delays or prevents atomic rearrangements required for phase separation.
Retention of lattice strain above a critical threshold maintains the single-phase solid solution during high-temperature operation.
Lattice strain is the dominant kinetic barrier against diffusion-driven phase separation over 473–1923 K.
Nanoparticles retaining significant lattice strain through thermal cycling will remain a single-phase solid solution.
Marked strain relaxation at elevated temperature will correspond to the emergence of secondary phases.
The emergence of secondary diffraction peaks indicates phase separation.
Pre-annealing can produce a comparison sample with reduced initial lattice strain.
In situ synchrotron XRD and PDF analysis can monitor lattice-strain evolution and structural phase changes during thermal cycling.
The proposed behavior is expected only under inert or controlled atmospheres where oxidation and substrate effects do not dominate.
Similar resistance to phase segregation in high-strain and strain-relaxed samples would falsify lattice strain as the dominant kinetic barrier.
Phase separation in the high-strain sample without prior strain relaxation would falsify lattice strain as the dominant kinetic barrier.
